source.author: cic
source.text: converti enim ex Atticis duorum eloquentissimorum nobilissimas orationes inter seque contrarias, Aeschini et Demostheni; nec converti ut interpres, sed ut orator, sententiis isdem et earum formis tamquam figuris, verbis ad nostram consuetudinem aptis.
source.text_original: converti enim ex Atticis duorum eloquentissimorum nobilissimas orationes inter seque contrarias, Aeschini et Demostheni; nec converti ut interpres, sed ut orator, sententiis isdem et earum  formis tamquam figuris, verbis ad nostram consuetudinem aptis.
source.text_english: For I have translated from the Attic writers the noblest speeches of two most eloquent men, Aeschines and Demosthenes, and I have translated not as an interpreter, but as an orator, keeping the same ideas and their forms, as it were their figures, but with words adapted to our own usage.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: conuerti enim ex Atticis duorum eloquentissimorum nobilissimas orationes inter seque contrarias, Aeschini et Demosthenis, nec conuerti ut interpres, sed ut orator, sententiis isdem et earum formis tam quam figuris, uerbis ad nostram consuetudinem aptis.
reuse.text_original: conuerti enim ex Atticis duorum eloquentissimorum nobilissimas orationes inter seque contrarias, Aeschini et Demosthenis, nec conuerti ut interpres, sed ut orator, sententiis isdem et earum formis tam quam figuris, uerbis ad nostram consuetudinem aptis.
reuse.text_english: For I have translated from the Attic writers the most famous speeches of two most eloquent men, Aeschines and Demosthenes, which are opposed to one another, and I have translated not as an interpreter but as an orator, keeping the same thoughts and their shapes as if they were figures, with words adapted to our own usage.
